name: Antinuous
long_description:
Antinuous is building the platform to run 100x more research, experiments, and simulations, 1,000x cheaper.

The platform combines a research agent, compute clusters, and hardware-tuned simulation software to give every agent access to research primitives that are typically reserved for massive R&D orgs, saving days per week on research iteration.
one_liner: Autonomous research agents for R&D and applied science

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We started as Salesgraph, building agents and workflows for enterprise sales teams. After OpenAI approached us to build the sales plugin ecosystem for ChatGPT, I declined the offer to build Antinuous.

We were working on sales execution first: going from first call booked to negotiation. We solved that internally at Mintlify. After we started tackling pipeline generation, we realized that pipeline generation tools make great primitives for all research. Agents that run, thousands at a time, digging through the world’s public data to find the one key insight that helps you close a deal.

You learn the industry that your pipeline is built on, map vertical bottlenecks to your solution, go deep on each person to see how they relate to you.

But what if you expand this past sales?

What if you’re in manufacturing and want to map supply chain bottlenecks to do better capacity planning?

What if you’re in finance and want to see what data-center construction is doing to grid prices in Texas and Louisiana?

What if you’re in R&D at a biotech and want to run virtual simulations overnight without hooking it up to your lab equipment.

This tool that we built for a niche use case of account research and pipeline generation turns out to be the perfect primitive for all research.

What if we built the best tools for agents to be able to run simulations, experiments, and research in collaboration autonomously.

Agents can divide up work from a set of constraints, run thousands of experiments in parallel, and iterate until achieving a better design, creating a massive data flywheel in the process that improves the agent, the tools, and the underlying models over time.

In testing, we’ve built a full digital twin of an F1 car, more efficient datacenter cooling with an early partner, and a fine-tuned classifier that they use to help route requests to the right model.

We’re building for the next trillion agents that need access to the same core primitives that research institutions have spent decades building out.

launches.title: Antinuous - 100x more experiments, 1,000x cheaper
launches.tagline: Antinuous is building the primitives and orchestration to allow anybody to run 100x more research, simulations, and experiments 1,000x cheaper.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**: We’re building an agent that can build, scaffold, and run experiments and simulations much faster and cheaper than frontier models can do on their own, and offering primitives (compute clusters, agent swarm orchestration, and simulation software/kernels) to all agents via A2A.

<https://youtu.be/nFBsPCOLD14>

---

We’re building the platform to run 100x more experiments and simulations, 1,000x cheaper.

Currently, frontier research is accelerating at a rate we’ve never seen before, but the acceleration is limited to those who have access to one of these three things:

1. Unrestricted access to frontier models
2. Exotic lab equipment at a well-funded institution, or
3. Expensive supercomputers with clusters of high-performance compute.

Frontier research labs and AI labs have all three.

Leading universities have one or two.

The vast majority of people on earth have 0.

We’re building a future where every single human has access to all three.

We’re tackling the problem in three ways.

Firstly, we’re building an agent purpose-built for research collaboration. One that has the tools and knowhow to run incredibly complex, multi-step PhD level research on any field.

Secondly, we’re giving each agent access to supercomputer clusters that they can spin up and down.

And finally, we’re building the next generation of simulation software designed to be run by thousands of agents working in parallel.

First, our agent.

The Antinuous agent is built from the ground up for research.

It has access to every tool you would expect a frontier research lab to include virtually.

Private and public data indexes, automations, modeling, data analysis, virtual simulation execution, coding, and more.

Agent swarms can be spun up to leverage massively parallel execution to speed up its work.

Every agent in a swarm can explore new ideas and chain together ideas that would take humans months to work through.

Secondly, compute.

Antinuous agents can leverage high performance computing resources like GPU clusters or high-speed interconnected CPU clusters just like you’d see at a trading firm or research lab.

They can do things like simulate physics, backtest trading strategies, fine-tune a specialized model, or simulate a group of humans in a real-world social scenario, all in clusters of compute we manage.

And finally, software.

To better leverage these compute clusters, we’re building the new frontier for simulation software purpose-built for agent experimentation.

Existing software exists for things like fluid dynamics, collisions, protein folding, genomics, backtesting, and many more.

The leading software applications for every field require seat by seat licenses and were built over many years to be clicked through by humans.

We think the next generation of simulations needs a stronger foundation to build on.

One that is flexible so that it can be extended with code for every use case it runs.

Elastic so that you can spin up thousands of instances across thousands of agents without paying for thousands of seats.

And programmable so that you can script it to run without human involvement, speeding up the feedback loop.

Our platform already runs research workflows today for researchers, analysts, and engineers at Stanford, OpenAI, Nvidia, Morgan Stanley, and more.

We’re excited to open it up to the public to see what you can discover.

Try it for free and give us feedback at [antinuous.com](http://antinuous.com).
